  "narrative_text": "A cross-paradigm metabolomics analysis of eight significantly altered metabolites revealed a dominant perturbation in tryptophan metabolism, confirmed across three complementary paradigms. RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit (FDR = 1.08e-15, fold enrichment 857.8) with six metabolites matched (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, tryptamine, quinolinic acid). The driver metabolites L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and quinolinic acid are documented as members of KEGG:hsa00380 via the PSEA metabolites_hit field. L-Proline maps to the urea-cycle and arginine-and-proline metabolic routes reported by Mummichog but does not participate in tryptophan metabolism. react_result.final_narrative_text: A cross-paradigm metabolomics analysis of eight significantly altered metabolites revealed a dominant perturbation in tryptophan metabolism, confirmed across three complementary paradigms. RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit (FDR = 1.08e-15, fold enrichment 857.8) with six metabolites matched (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, tryptamine, quinolinic acid). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently returned KEGG:hsa00380 as rank 1 (p = 1.79e-07), and Mummichog m/z-network analysis returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as rank 0 (p = 8.40e-05). This three-method convergence establishes tryptophan catabolism as the primary affected pathway. Within this umbrella, two sub-branches are strongly supported: the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR = 6.49e-09) captures the kynurenine-branch conversion of L-tryptophan to quinolinic acid via 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, with molybdenum as a cofactor; and the Reactome Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis pathway (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR = 1.39e-08) captures the parallel serotonergic branch producing serotonin and melatonin. The driver metabolites L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and quinolinic acid are documented as members of KEGG:hsa00380 via the PSEA metabolites_hit field. L-Proline maps to the urea-cycle and arginine-and-proline metabolic routes reported by Mummichog but does not participate in tryptophan metabolism. Molybdenum is a cofactor in both the tryptophan pathway's quinolinic acid arm and general amino-acid metabolism.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: A cross-paradigm metabolomics analysis of eight significantly altered metabolites revealed a dominant perturbation in tryptophan metabolism, confirmed across three complementary paradigms. RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit (FDR = 1.08e-15, fold enrichment 857.8) with six metabolites matched (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, tryptamine, quinolinic acid). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently returned KEGG:hsa00380 as rank 1 (p = 1.79e-07), and Mummichog m/z-network analysis returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as rank 0 (p = 8.40e-05). This three-method convergence establishes tryptophan catabolism as the primary affected pathway. Within this umbrella, two sub-branches are strongly supported: the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR = 6.49e-09) captures the kynurenine-branch conversion of L-tryptophan to quinolinic acid via 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, with molybdenum as a cofactor; and the Reactome Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis pathway (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR = 1.39e-08) captures the parallel serotonergic branch producing serotonin and melatonin. The driver metabolites L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and quinolinic acid are documented as members of KEGG:hsa00380 via the PSEA metabolites_hit field. L-Proline maps to the urea-cycle and arginine-and-proline metabolic routes reported by Mummichog but does not participate in tryptophan metabolism. Molybdenum is a cofactor in both the tryptophan pathway's quinolinic acid arm and general amino-acid metabolism.
